trigger: application needs visibility into accepted and rejected VPC traffic
correct: Enable VPC Flow Logs and analyze with CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Athena
why: Flow Logs provide network-flow metadata for diagnosis and capacity analysis.

trigger: container tasks should scale with request or queue metrics
correct: Use ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking or step scaling
why: Service Auto Scaling adjusts task desired count from CloudWatch metrics.
distractors: Resize one task manually every day

trigger: container launches are slow due to large images
correct: Use smaller layered images, regional ECR, and image caching or SOCI where applicable
why: Optimized images and pull mechanisms reduce startup time.
distractors: Add unused packages to the image
Use an EBS snapshot as registry

objective: Run bursty containers without host management
trigger: short-lived container jobs need elastic compute
correct: Use ECS on Fargate or AWS Batch according to job orchestration needs
why: Managed compute removes server provisioning and scales per task or job.
distractors: Maintain fixed oversized EC2 hosts only

trigger: EKS workload needs pod and infrastructure elasticity
correct: Use HPA or KEDA for pods and Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter for nodes
why: Separate pod and node scaling responds to workload and scheduling demand.
distractors: Use only a larger control plane

trigger: container services need dynamic private discovery
correct: Use AWS Cloud Map or ECS Service Connect
why: Managed discovery tracks changing task endpoints and provides service connectivity.
distractors: Use public DNS for every internal request

trigger: on-premises NFS data needs accelerated parallel migration
correct: Use AWS DataSync with an agent near the source
why: DataSync parallelizes and optimizes network transfer with verification.

trigger: Windows file shares need migration to S3, EFS, or FSx
correct: Use AWS DataSync with an SMB location and required agent
why: DataSync supports SMB transfers and preserves selected metadata.

objective: Move data between AWS storage services
trigger: large recurring AWS-to-AWS storage transfer needs managed scheduling and verification
correct: Use AWS DataSync; an agent is often unnecessary for supported AWS service pairs
why: DataSync manages transfer tasks and validation within the AWS network.
distractors: Download and upload through a laptop

trigger: database migration full load is slower than required
correct: Tune replication capacity, parallel load settings, table mappings, and target indexes based on documentation
why: DMS throughput depends on replication resources, source, target, network, and task settings.

trigger: ongoing replication lags behind source changes
correct: Monitor CDCLatencySource and CDCLatencyTarget, size capacity, and address source or target bottlenecks
why: The latency metrics separate capture delay from target-apply delay.

trigger: fault-tolerant flexible jobs can be interrupted
correct: Use EC2 Spot Instances or AWS Batch with Spot
why: Spot uses spare capacity at steep discounts for interruption-tolerant work.
distractors: Use On-Demand only without evaluating flexibility

trigger: baseline compute is predictable for one or three years
correct: Purchase Savings Plans or Reserved Instances according to flexibility needs
why: Commitment discounts reduce cost for predictable usage.
distractors: Use Spot for a noninterruptible singleton without recovery

trigger: nonproduction instances are used only during business hours
correct: Schedule start and stop and use rightsizing recommendations
why: Turning off idle compute eliminates unnecessary runtime charges.
distractors: Use Multi-AZ solely for cost reduction

trigger: small workload has low average CPU with occasional bursts
correct: Use a burstable T-family instance when credit behavior fits
why: Burstable instances are cost-effective for low baseline utilization.

trigger: commercial software licensing requires host affinity or BYOL control
correct: Evaluate Dedicated Hosts and license-aware placement when required
why: Dedicated Hosts can support eligible per-socket or per-core licensing models.
distractors: Use a NAT gateway for licensing

trigger: data retained for years and rarely retrieved
correct: Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive
why: Deep Archive offers the lowest S3 storage cost with long retrieval times.

trigger: object access frequency changes unpredictably
correct: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering
why: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves eligible objects among access tiers.
distractors: Use One Zone-IA for irreplaceable data automatically

trigger: objects become less frequently accessed over time
correct: Use an S3 Lifecycle configuration
why: Lifecycle rules transition or expire objects based on age and other filters.
distractors: Run a daily EC2 script to copy all objects manually

objective: Reduce cost for reproducible infrequent data
trigger: data can be recreated and does not require multi-AZ resilience
correct: Use S3 One Zone-IA when retrieval and minimum-duration charges fit
why: One Zone-IA costs less by storing data in one AZ.
distractors: Use it for the only copy of critical backups
Use S3 Standard for known archival only

trigger: millions of tiny objects are expensive to transition and retrieve
correct: Aggregate objects or evaluate storage-class minimum size and duration economics
why: Request and minimum-size charges can dominate small-object storage cost.
distractors: Transition every tiny temporary object immediately without analysis

trigger: table traffic is unpredictable and often low
correct: Use on-demand capacity and evaluate auto scaling or reserved capacity for stable workloads
why: Capacity mode should match predictability and utilization.

trigger: development database has long idle periods
correct: Use Aurora Serverless v2 scaling and supported minimum capacity, or schedule/stop eligible databases
why: Elastic capacity or stopping reduces idle database cost.
distractors: Run the largest provisioned cluster continuously

trigger: database writer is oversized because of read traffic
correct: Use read replicas or caching and rightsize the writer
why: Separating reads or caching can avoid scaling the primary vertically.
distractors: Enable Multi-AZ only and expect read scaling on passive standby

trigger: Aurora workload has high I/O charges and predictable characteristics
correct: Compare Aurora Standard and I/O-Optimized using measured I/O cost
why: I/O-Optimized can lower total cost for I/O-intensive workloads.
distractors: Always choose one model regardless of workload

trigger: old manual snapshots accumulate indefinitely
correct: Apply retention governance and delete unneeded manual snapshots after validation
why: Manual snapshots persist and incur storage until deleted.

objective: Avoid NAT charges for AWS services
trigger: private workloads access S3 or DynamoDB frequently
correct: Use gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB
why: Gateway endpoints avoid NAT processing and internet paths.
distractors: Assign public IPs to all instances

trigger: private subnets in many AZs use one NAT gateway
correct: Use a NAT gateway in each AZ with same-AZ routing
why: This avoids cross-AZ data transfer and improves resilience.
distractors: Send every AZ through one remote NAT gateway
Put NAT gateway in a private subnet

trigger: global users download repeated content
correct: Use CloudFront caching
why: CloudFront reduces origin egress and can have favorable transfer pricing.
distractors: Serve every request directly from EC2

trigger: large steady on-premises traffic uses internet egress
correct: Evaluate Direct Connect pricing and keep resources in appropriate regions
why: Dedicated connectivity and regional placement can reduce transfer cost at scale.

trigger: chatty tiers are deployed in different regions without a resilience requirement
correct: Co-locate tightly coupled tiers in the same region and often the same AZ where resilience permits
why: Inter-region and cross-AZ traffic can add transfer charges.
distractors: Scatter all components globally by default
Use Global Accelerator for internal database calls

trigger: function duration and memory are inefficient
correct: Use AWS Lambda Power Tuning and optimize code, memory, and architecture
why: Benchmarking identifies the lowest-cost configuration for required performance.
distractors: Always select maximum memory without measuring
Keep idle EC2 hosts for every function

trigger: compute workload can run on Arm architecture
correct: Use Graviton-based EC2, RDS, or container compute where supported
why: Graviton often provides better price-performance for compatible workloads.

trigger: large stable container service runs continuously
correct: Compare Fargate Savings Plans, Graviton, and EC2 capacity for the utilization pattern
why: Steady workloads may benefit from commitments or EC2-based density.
distractors: Use only Fargate Spot for noninterruptible critical tasks
Use one task per host with no bin packing

trigger: interruptible container workers process queued jobs
correct: Use Fargate Spot with standard Fargate fallback where needed
why: Fargate Spot reduces compute cost for interruption-tolerant tasks.
distractors: Use it for singleton stateful databases

trigger: low-traffic API does not justify always-on servers
correct: Use API Gateway with Lambda or another pay-per-use integration
why: Serverless request-based pricing avoids idle instance cost.
distractors: Run a large fixed fleet continuously

trigger: volumes have unused capacity or overprovisioned performance
correct: Use CloudWatch and Compute Optimizer guidance, then modify volume type, size, IOPS, or throughput
why: EBS elastic volumes allow tuning without replacing the instance in many cases.

trigger: file system has bursty or predictable throughput
correct: Select elastic, bursting, or provisioned throughput based on measured workload
why: Correct throughput mode avoids overpaying while meeting demand.

trigger: most files become infrequently accessed
correct: Enable EFS lifecycle management to IA or Archive classes
why: Lifecycle management reduces cost for cold file data.
distractors: Copy files manually to instance store

trigger: many teams retain snapshots indefinitely
correct: Use AWS Backup policies and lifecycle rules to cold storage or expiration
why: Central policies enforce consistent retention and reduce sprawl.

trigger: multiple overlapping backup tools protect the same resources
correct: Inventory recovery requirements and consolidate schedules in AWS Backup where suitable
why: Removing redundant copies lowers storage cost without sacrificing defined recovery objectives.
distractors: Keep every tool at maximum retention

trigger: teams must know before monthly spend exceeds limits
correct: Use AWS Budgets with actual and forecast alerts
why: Budgets tracks spend and usage against thresholds.

trigger: unexpected service-level spending must be identified automatically
correct: Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
why: The service models normal spend and alerts on unusual changes.

trigger: finance needs account, service, tag, and usage-level cost analysis
correct: Enable the Cost and Usage Report and query it with Athena or another analytics tool
why: CUR provides the most detailed billing and usage data.
distractors: Use only the EC2 console total

trigger: business units need chargeback by workload
correct: Use enforced cost allocation tags and account or organizational structure
why: Consistent tags and accounts map usage to owners.

trigger: resources are consistently underutilized
correct: Use AWS Compute Optimizer and validate recommendations against workload requirements
why: Compute Optimizer analyzes metrics and recommends resource shapes.
distractors: Resize solely from one CPU sample

trigger: moderate dataset fits migration window over available network
correct: Use AWS DataSync and schedule transfers
why: DataSync avoids appliance shipping when bandwidth and time are sufficient.
distractors: Use Snowball for a few gigabytes by default

trigger: very large dataset cannot finish over the network in time
correct: Use AWS Snowball Edge or another Snow Family option
why: Offline appliances can be cheaper and faster than prolonged network transfer.

trigger: database is large and business downtime is expensive
correct: Use DMS full load plus CDC and perform a controlled cutover
why: Ongoing replication reduces the final outage window.
distractors: Stop the source for the entire multi-day copy

trigger: migration task has long idle periods or uncertain capacity needs
correct: Evaluate AWS DMS Serverless or rightsize replication instances
why: Elastic or right-sized replication avoids paying for unnecessary capacity.
distractors: Always choose the largest replication instance

trigger: DMS replication and staging resources are no longer required
correct: Validate cutover, then stop or delete unneeded replication resources and snapshots according to retention policy
why: Migration infrastructure continues incurring charges after project completion.

objective: Choose managed services to reduce operations
trigger: small team cannot maintain undifferentiated infrastructure
correct: Use managed or serverless services when their total cost is lower
why: Total cost includes labor, patching, availability engineering, and idle capacity.
distractors: Choose self-managed clusters solely on hourly price

trigger: workload has no regional RTO requirement but is duplicated globally
correct: Use Multi-AZ in one region and add multi-region only when justified by requirements
why: Regional duplication adds compute, storage, data-transfer, and operational cost.
distractors: Use one AZ only for all critical workloads

trigger: business specifies relaxed RTO and RPO
correct: Choose backup-and-restore, pilot light, warm standby, or active-active based on measured objectives
why: DR cost rises as RTO and RPO become more aggressive.

trigger: backend repeatedly computes identical results
correct: Add a suitable cache and rightsize backend capacity
why: Caching can reduce expensive repeated compute and database work.
distractors: Scale every backend to maximum size

objective: Use lifecycle cleanup for temporary resources
trigger: ephemeral artifacts and logs accumulate
correct: Apply expiration policies and automated cleanup with safeguards
why: Automated retention prevents indefinite storage growth.

trigger: administrators must use a second factor before sensitive API calls
correct: Use IAM policy conditions that require aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent and enforce MFA-enabled access paths
why: MFA conditions can deny privileged actions when the session lacks MFA context.

trigger: developers may create roles but must not exceed an approved permission ceiling
correct: Require a permissions boundary on delegated IAM roles
why: A permissions boundary limits the maximum effective permissions of roles users create.
distractors: Use an SCP only inside one IAM user

trigger: third-party SaaS assumes a customer role across many accounts
correct: Require a unique external ID in the role trust policy
why: The external ID helps prevent another customer from tricking the third party into assuming the role.
distractors: Use an Elastic IP allowlist only

trigger: temporary privileged sessions must expire quickly
correct: Set the role maximum session duration and request an appropriately short session
why: STS role credentials expire automatically according to configured session limits.
distractors: Store access keys in Secrets Manager forever

trigger: authorization depends on department and project attributes from the identity provider
correct: Use session tags and ABAC policies
why: Session tags carry identity attributes into policy evaluation for attribute-based access control.
distractors: Create one IAM user per attribute combination
Use security groups for business attributes

trigger: organization requires encryption under application-controlled keys before data reaches AWS
correct: Use client-side encryption with an approved key-management process
why: Client-side encryption protects data before transmission and leaves key control with the application.

trigger: a KMS key should decrypt only objects from a particular S3 bucket
correct: Use KMS encryption-context conditions in the key policy
why: Encryption context can bind cryptographic authorization to expected resource metadata.
distractors: Use only the key alias name

objective: Separate key administration from key use
trigger: security administrators manage keys but application operators may encrypt and decrypt
correct: Use distinct KMS key administrators and key users in the key policy
why: Separation of duties prevents key administrators from automatically receiving data-use permission.

trigger: applications retrieve credentials but must not expose them in logs
correct: Retrieve secrets at runtime and redact secret values from application and tracing logs
why: Runtime retrieval and redaction reduce credential persistence and leakage.
distractors: Store the secret in user data
Put the secret in a public parameter

trigger: security team needs continuous identification of storage resources without encryption
correct: Use AWS Config managed rules and Security Hub findings
why: Config and Security Hub can identify and aggregate encryption-compliance findings.

trigger: API Gateway must validate JWTs issued by a managed user directory
correct: Use an API Gateway JWT or Cognito user-pool authorizer
why: The authorizer validates tokens before the request reaches the backend.
distractors: Create IAM users for every public user

trigger: public API needs per-client quotas and rate controls
correct: Use API Gateway usage plans, API keys where appropriate, and throttling
why: Usage plans and throttling constrain request volume; keys identify consuming applications rather than provide full authentication.
distractors: Use security groups on public clients

trigger: distributed web tier needs server-side session storage with expiration
correct: Use ElastiCache or DynamoDB with encryption, least privilege, and TTL as appropriate
why: A managed shared store avoids local-session dependence and can enforce automatic expiration.
distractors: Store sessions on instance store only
Put session IDs in public S3 objects

trigger: organization must block vulnerable or unapproved images
correct: Use ECR image scanning and deployment-policy controls
why: ECR scanning identifies vulnerabilities and pipeline controls can prevent promotion of failing images.

trigger: ECS tasks need database credentials without putting them in task-definition plaintext
correct: Reference Secrets Manager or Parameter Store secrets from the task definition and grant the task role access
why: ECS can inject or retrieve managed secrets while IAM limits access.
distractors: Use the execution-role access key in code

trigger: security team needs one place for findings from multiple AWS security services
correct: Use AWS Security Hub with delegated administration and organization integration
why: Security Hub normalizes and aggregates supported findings across accounts and regions.

trigger: specific security findings should trigger repeatable corrective actions
correct: Use EventBridge with Systems Manager Automation or Lambda remediation targets
why: Event-driven remediation can respond consistently to findings.
distractors: Wait for a monthly manual review

trigger: incident responder needs identity, source IP, time, and request parameters
correct: Search CloudTrail Lake or centralized CloudTrail logs
why: CloudTrail records the API caller and request context needed for investigation.
distractors: Use VPC Flow Logs alone for API identity

trigger: audit logs must be protected against alteration for years
correct: Store them in a dedicated S3 bucket with Object Lock, versioning, encryption, and restrictive policies
why: Immutable storage and account separation protect evidentiary logs.
distractors: Store only on EC2 root volumes
Allow all administrators to delete logs

trigger: organization needs findings for public buckets, snapshots, and other exposed resources
correct: Use IAM Access Analyzer and Security Hub or Config controls
why: Access Analyzer identifies resource policies that grant external access.

trigger: on-premises network needs encrypted connectivity to a VPC over the internet
correct: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN with redundant tunnels
why: Site-to-Site VPN provides IPsec-encrypted tunnels and redundant endpoints.
distractors: Use Direct Connect without MACsec or VPN and assume encryption

trigger: private circuit traffic requires encryption in transit
correct: Use MACsec on supported Direct Connect connections or a VPN over Direct Connect
why: Direct Connect is private but not inherently encrypted; MACsec or IPsec adds encryption.
distractors: Use a security group as link encryption

trigger: workloads may access only approved external domains
correct: Use AWS Network Firewall domain-list rules and controlled egress routing
why: Managed firewall rules can filter outbound traffic by domain and protocol.
distractors: Use IAM policies to filter arbitrary internet domains

trigger: public hosted zone needs signed DNS responses
correct: Enable DNSSEC signing in Route 53 and configure the parent delegation
why: DNSSEC lets resolvers validate authenticity of DNS records.
distractors: Use ACM certificates for DNS responses

trigger: private endpoint should allow only approved actions and resources
correct: Apply a restrictive VPC endpoint policy in addition to identity and resource policies
why: Endpoint policies add a control layer for traffic using the endpoint.

trigger: live migration has reached low CDC latency and applications must move safely
correct: Quiesce writes, allow DMS to catch up, validate, then redirect applications to the target
why: A controlled cutover avoids lost writes and confirms target consistency.
distractors: Redirect while source writes continue with no coordination
Stop the replication task before it catches up

trigger: migration team must confirm source and target rows match
correct: Enable AWS DMS data validation and monitor validation statistics
why: DMS validation compares migrated data and reports mismatches.

trigger: long-running migration must tolerate replication-host failure
correct: Use a Multi-AZ DMS replication configuration or suitable serverless architecture
why: Multi-AZ replication capacity reduces interruption from infrastructure failure.
distractors: Run one undersized single-AZ instance with no restart plan

trigger: large file migration may be interrupted and must continue efficiently
correct: Rerun the DataSync task so it transfers changed or missing data and verifies according to task settings
why: DataSync incremental behavior avoids retransferring unchanged files unnecessarily.

trigger: file systems require nightly incremental synchronization
correct: Create a DataSync task with a schedule and monitoring
why: Scheduled tasks automate recurring transfer and verification.
distractors: Use an IAM user cron key

trigger: message delivery can be repeated after retries
correct: Design consumers with idempotency keys or conditional writes
why: Idempotent processing prevents duplicate delivery from causing duplicate business effects.
distractors: Assume every distributed message arrives exactly once

objective: Select a safe SQS visibility timeout
trigger: consumer processing sometimes takes several minutes
correct: Set visibility timeout longer than normal processing and extend it when needed
why: The timeout prevents another consumer from receiving a message still being processed.

trigger: event consumers may be unavailable for hours
correct: Use durable queues or streams with sufficient retention
why: Retention allows consumers to catch up after recovery.

trigger: downstream service failures cause cascading request exhaustion
correct: Implement timeouts, bounded retries with jitter, and circuit-breaker behavior
why: These patterns stop repeated failing calls from consuming all resources.

trigger: noncritical dependency is unavailable but core application should remain usable
correct: Use cached or stale data and feature isolation where business rules permit
why: Graceful degradation preserves core capability during partial failures.
distractors: Fail the entire application for every optional dependency

trigger: regional recovery needs repeatable resource creation
correct: Use infrastructure as code with tested deployment pipelines
why: Versioned templates make recovery repeatable and reduce manual configuration drift.
distractors: Store configuration only on one laptop
Use an Elastic IP as the DR plan

trigger: instances must be rebuilt with application and configuration dependencies
correct: Maintain patched AMIs plus bootstrapping and externalized configuration
why: Golden images and automation reduce recovery time while avoiding unique pets.
distractors: Make manual changes directly on every server

trigger: business must verify stated RTO and RPO
correct: Run scheduled recovery exercises and measure actual results
why: Only testing verifies that backups, automation, and dependencies meet recovery objectives.

objective: Preserve application state during AZ loss
trigger: stateful service uses local data but must survive host and AZ failure
correct: Replicate state to a multi-AZ managed data store or application-level replicas
why: State must exist outside a single host and AZ to survive failure.
distractors: Store the only copy on instance store

trigger: critical DNS configuration must be auditable and reproducible
correct: Manage records with infrastructure as code and retain CloudTrail history
why: Versioned definitions and audit history enable rapid restoration of DNS configuration.

trigger: application needs data structures, replication, and persistence options
correct: Use ElastiCache for Redis or MemoryDB according to durability requirements
why: Redis-compatible services support rich data structures and low-latency access.
distractors: Use Memcached for persistence and replication requirements

objective: Select Memcached for simple scale-out cache
trigger: application needs a simple multithreaded ephemeral object cache
correct: Use ElastiCache for Memcached
why: Memcached provides simple distributed caching without Redis persistence features.
distractors: Use RDS Multi-AZ as a cache

trigger: many clients request the same expired key simultaneously
correct: Use TTL jitter, request coalescing, or stale-while-revalidate patterns
why: These patterns prevent synchronized misses from overwhelming the backend.
distractors: Set every key to expire at the same instant

trigger: batch analytics must read an entire large table faster
correct: Use parallel Scan with controlled segments and capacity impact
why: Parallel scan can increase throughput but consumes significant read capacity and is not a substitute for key-based queries.
distractors: Use parallel scan for every online request

trigger: high-throughput applications need fast connection recovery
correct: Use RDS Proxy or cluster-aware drivers with retries and appropriate DNS handling
why: Connection management and topology awareness reduce disruption after failover.

trigger: high-throughput traffic between compatible VPC resources needs lower packet overhead
correct: Use jumbo frames end to end only where every path component supports the MTU
why: A consistent larger MTU reduces packet overhead; mismatches cause fragmentation or drops.
distractors: Set a larger MTU on one endpoint only

trigger: load balancer should distribute to healthy targets across enabled AZs
correct: Configure targets and cross-zone behavior appropriate to the load balancer type and cost model
why: Correct zonal configuration balances traffic while considering cross-AZ charges.
distractors: Register targets in one AZ only
Use a single Elastic IP as load balancing

objective: Choose NLB for extreme connection performance
trigger: application needs static IP support and layer-4 high throughput
correct: Use a Network Load Balancer
why: NLB handles TCP, TLS, and UDP at high scale with zonal static IP capabilities.
distractors: Use API Gateway for arbitrary UDP
Use an ALB for source-IP preservation in every protocol without analysis

trigger: application needs host, path, header, or method-based routing
correct: Use an Application Load Balancer
why: ALB provides layer-7 routing and integrates with web-oriented targets.

trigger: frequent on-premises DNS queries resolve private AWS names
correct: Deploy redundant Route 53 Resolver endpoints in suitable subnets and cache responses on-premises
why: Redundant endpoints and local caching improve DNS availability and latency.
distractors: Send every query to a public resolver

trigger: teams must not launch disallowed expensive instance families
correct: Use SCPs, IAM conditions, and service quotas as preventive controls
why: Preventive controls reduce accidental spend before resources are created.

trigger: flexible workload can run in multiple regions with different prices
correct: Compare regional service, data-transfer, and compliance costs before placement
why: AWS prices and transfer patterns vary by region, but requirements must remain satisfied.
distractors: Choose the farthest region solely for a lower instance price

trigger: verbose application logs create large CloudWatch charges
correct: Set appropriate log levels, retention, filtering, and archival strategy
why: Controlling volume and retention reduces ingestion and storage without losing required observability.

trigger: steady compute spans EC2, Fargate, and Lambda
correct: Evaluate a Compute Savings Plan for broad eligible usage flexibility
why: Compute Savings Plans apply across multiple compute services and instance choices.
distractors: Buy Dedicated Hosts for serverless usage

trigger: detached volumes, idle load balancers, and unused IPs continue billing
correct: Use tagging, Config, Trusted Advisor, and automation to find and remove verified orphaned resources
why: Lifecycle governance prevents forgotten resources from accumulating charges.
distractors: Delete all resources without ownership checks
